condition: suspected ruptured ectopic pregnancy presenting with acute severe unilateral lower abdominal pain
level_rationale: Sudden severe right lower abdominal pain today at 7 weeks gestation indicates suspected ectopic pregnancy requiring immediate emergency hospital evaluation to rule out tubal rupture, whereas isolated burning urination today at 7 weeks pregnancy leaves no peritoneal or hemorrhagic red flags and warrants outpatient prenatal or primary-care clinic urine testing and oral antibiotic therapy.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain pregnant-speaker everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + causal belief-addition clause (-att) + single-symptom uncomplicated dysuria outpatient clinic control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age and sex, 7 weeks pregnancy, and today's acute severe right lower abdominal pain) with a 1-word span difference (14 vs 15 words) and 8 shared trailing tokens ('today so I need to go to the'). Swapping only f3 to burning urination shifts care from emergency hospital evaluation (level 4) to outpatient clinic urine culture and oral antibiotic care (level 2) with zero residual red flags and zero stated negatives.
